answer: Similarity splitting: each epoch the network embeds every answer and clusters near-duplicates, the way you'd spot one vine snaking through every bed of a garden. All answers in a cluster split a single reward. A sybil farm running one model behind 100 accounts produces look-alike text and earns roughly one share, not 100. To earn more it must pay for genuinely distinct work per account, so its costs climb while its payout stays flat as marble.
